summary: The note surveys Boston's infrastructure development initiatives launched after September 2023, covering transportation, public spaces, utilities and broadband, financing, and community engagement. It describes how the city tries to balance heritage preservation with modernization, citing a five-year plan by Mayor Julia Espinoza and ongoing projects such as the Logan Airport expansion and Dorchester Bay revitalization.
one_line: Overview of Boston's post-September 2023 infrastructure plans across transit, parks, utilities, financing and community input, balancing heritage preservation with modernization.
key_facts: Boston's public works history dates to 1716 with America's first lighthouse on Little Brewster Island.
On September 15, 2023, Mayor Julia Espinoza released a five-year plan addressing Boston's most urgent infrastructure needs.

On November 2, 2023, Director Thomas McAllister of the Boston Transportation Department unveiled a transportation vision including expanded MBTA access, more eco-friendly buses, and a bridge and tunnel improvement program.
The transportation plan sets an explicit goal of doubling dedicated bike lanes by 2025.
On October 1, 2023, Commissioner Luisa Rodriguez of the Department of Parks and Recreation announced a revitalization initiative for Boston's parks and public spaces.
The 'Green Ribbon' proposal seeks an uninterrupted network of green paths serving recreation and acting as wildlife corridors within the city.
Kyle Hendricks' office of Chief Information Officer leads high-speed broadband initiatives, prioritizing fiber-optic networks starting December 2023 to bridge the digital divide.
Boston is modernizing its 19th-century sewer system in the North End, its oldest residential neighborhood, blending new technology with historical architecture.
City Treasurer Angela Park's administrators use municipal bonds, state and federal grants, and public-private partnerships to finance projects.
On January 10, 2024, Angela Park announced a partnership with several private investors for public works financing.
Community input forums began on September 20, 2023 and have continued regularly since.
The Logan International Airport expansion is set for 2026, with groundbreaking on February 9.
Starting March 2024, the Boston Coastal Development Authority and environmental experts began revitalizing the Dorchester Bay area with ecological preservation techniques.
